investment_summary:
Meta's 2025 results show a strong core business. Revenue grew 22% to $200.97 billion on 12% more ad impressions and a 9% higher price per ad [1]. Profit lagged: net income fell 3% after a $15.93 billion tax charge, and free cash flow fell 16% to $43.59 billion as capex nearly doubled [1].

Consensus data, dated after the 10-K, has turned negative on near-term earnings. FY2026 EPS estimates fell 8.5% over 90 days, and the June and September 2026 quarters missed by 14.4% and 29.3% [3]. Consensus still expects revenue growth of 27.8% in FY2026 and 21.9% in FY2027 [3].

Valuation is the key question. The reverse DCF [2][3] implies 17.7% annual revenue growth for ten years, close to the 19.9% three-year historical CAGR and well above the fading consensus path. On that path the implied return is 9.7%, below the 11.2% WACC, so the price requires growth to stay near its historical pace. Main risks are the $19.19 billion Reality Labs loss and $115–135 billion of 2026 capex guidance [1].
key_takeaways: Ad pricing and reach should keep driving growth, as 12% more impressions and a 9% higher price per ad lifted revenue 22% [1].
Free cash flow should lag growth, because capex nearly doubled to $72.22 billion and 2026 guidance is $115–135 billion [1].
The stock looks fully priced: the current enterprise value needs 17.7% revenue growth for a decade, while the consensus path returns 9.7%, below WACC [2][3].
Reality Labs' $19.19 billion loss is the main earnings drag; we see EPS risk until its AI payoff is visible [1][3].
business_overview:
Meta Platforms is a social technology company. Its Family of Apps includes Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads, WhatsApp and Meta AI, and its Reality Labs segment sells Meta Quest headsets and Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses [1]. Advertising generated $196.18 billion of the $200.97 billion total 2025 revenue, about 98% [1]. Family daily active people averaged 3.58 billion in December 2025, up 7%, and ad impressions rose 12% while the average price per ad rose 9% [1]. Other revenue, driven by WhatsApp paid messaging and Meta Verified, rose 50% to $2.58 billion [1].

The two segments differ sharply in economics. Family of Apps revenue rose 22% to $198.76 billion, and segment income from operations rose 18% to $102.47 billion, although its margin fell to 52% from 54% as costs rose 28% to $96.29 billion, mainly on employee compensation, infrastructure, partner arrangements and legal-related costs [1]. Reality Labs revenue grew only 3% to $2.21 billion, helped by AI glasses and partly offset by lower Meta Quest sales, while its operating loss widened 8% to $19.19 billion [1]. Management expects 2026 Reality Labs losses to remain similar to 2025 [1].

Strategy centres on AI. The company is investing across its discovery engine and ad tools and trains a mix of open and closed models, and in 2025 it launched Meta Ray-Ban Display with the Meta Neural Band [1]. Capital returns totalled $31.57 billion, including $26.26 billion of buybacks, and the quarterly dividend rose to $0.525 [1]. At a closing price of $667.01, the market value is about $1.87 trillion, with a 52-week range of $477.49 to $793.02 [2]. Consensus carries a Buy rating and a mean target of $842.54, with a range of $650 to $1,050 [3].
market_position:
Meta's end market is global, but growth varies by geography. Revenue grew 21% in the United States and Canada, 24% in Europe, 20% in Asia-Pacific and 27% in Rest of World in 2025 [1]. Impression growth is concentrated in Asia-Pacific, which monetizes at lower rates, so regional mix dilutes the average price per ad [1]. Within this peer set, Alphabet is the only peer of comparable business model at scale, and Meta's size sits between that group and the smaller social platforms [2].

Customers are advertisers rather than a concentrated list of named accounts. Marketers buy through a self-service platform, agencies and resellers, and the 10-K does not name major customers, disclose customer concentration or state a market share figure [1]. Demand is broad but short-cycle, because marketers have no long-term advertising commitments with the company [1]. The platform is also exposed to decisions by others: the filing names Apple and Google as operators that have changed iOS and browser rules, and the EU consent model limits targeting [1].

Meta's position rests on user reach. Its 3.58 billion average daily active people and its messaging services give it a base that few advertisers can replicate, although some products are not generally available in China [1]. Future growth depends on converting that reach into revenue at higher prices, and on new paid services such as WhatsApp messaging, which the filing says is monetized only in a limited fashion [1]. On FY2026 consensus, the shares trade at 21.0x forward earnings and 6.2x forward EV/Sales [3].
operating_results:
Revenue rose 22% to $200.97 billion in 2025, with advertising at $196.18 billion (+22%) on 12% more ad impressions and a 9% higher average price per ad [1]. Other revenue rose 50% to $2.58 billion [1]. Cost of revenue grew 20% but stayed at 18% of revenue, and gross margin edged up to 82.0% from 81.7% [1]. R&D was the largest cost increase, rising 31% to $57.37 billion on compensation and AI infrastructure [1].

Operating income rose 20% to $83.28 billion, but the operating margin slipped to 41% from 42% [1]. Net income fell 3% to $60.46 billion after a $15.93 billion One Big Beautiful Bill Act tax charge lifted the effective tax rate to 30%, so net margin dropped to 30% from 38% [1]. Diluted EPS fell 2% to $23.49, partly offset by a 1.5% lower diluted share count [1]. Operating cash flow rose 27% to $115.80 billion, but capital expenditures including finance lease principal nearly doubled to $72.22 billion, so free cash flow fell 16% to $43.59 billion [1].

The balance sheet grew faster than liquidity. Total assets rose 33% to $366.02 billion, total debt rose 71% to $83.90 billion, and long-term debt more than doubled to $58.74 billion [1]. Cash and securities were $81.59 billion, and the current ratio was 2.60x, down from 2.98x [1]. Off the balance sheet, leases not yet commenced total $103.77 billion and contractual commitments total $131.05 billion [1]. Since the 10-K, the position has tightened: at 2026-09-30, total debt was $114.84 billion, net cash was -$32.39 billion and trailing free cash flow was $28.65 billion [2]. Consensus expects FY2026 EPS of $29.01 [3].
risk_assessment:
Advertising concentration is the core risk. Substantially all revenue comes from advertising on Facebook and Instagram, and most of it comes from mobile devices [1]. Targeting and measurement are being narrowed by regulation and by platform operators: the 2021 iOS changes reduced targeting and measurement, and the filing says marketer reaction has negatively affected advertising revenue [1]. Marketers can move budgets within a quarter, so the revenue base is sensitive to cyclical and event-driven swings [1].

Regulation and litigation add a second layer. The European Commission's April 2025 final decision found the subscription-for-no-ads model non-compliant with the DMA, and Meta has appealed; the filing warns that further changes could materially worsen the European business [1]. Bellwether trials in youth-related litigation are scheduled for 2026 and beyond, and the company operates under an FTC consent order [1]. The 10-K gives no dollar amounts for fines or reserves, so these exposures cannot be sized from the filing [1].

Investment and funding risk is now the largest financial one. Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion in 2025, with similar losses expected in 2026, and capex guidance of $115 to $135 billion would require operating cash flow to grow far faster than its 27% rise in 2025 [1]. Net cash moved from -$2.31 billion at fiscal year-end to -$32.39 billion at 2026-09-30, and shares outstanding rose 1.4% year on year at that date [2]. Earnings have also disappointed: EPS missed estimates by 14.4% and 29.3% in the June and September 2026 quarters [3]. Financial quality scores are mixed: the Altman Z-Score is 8.30 and the Beneish M-Score is -3.01, but the Piotroski F-Score is 5 of 9 [2].
competitors_analysis:
Peers were chosen on business model first and size second. Alphabet is the closest model at scale, as an advertising-funded platform spending heavily on AI, but its revenue is 1.9 times Meta's [2][4]. Snap and Pinterest are ad-funded social platforms with a similar engagement-driven model, but they are far smaller, with 2025 revenue of $5.93 billion and $4.22 billion respectively [4]. Reddit and The Trade Desk were not chosen: Reddit is growing faster, and The Trade Desk is an ad-buying platform rather than an ad-funded network [2].

Meta leads the group on growth and margins. Its 2025 revenue growth of 22.2% was the highest, ahead of Pinterest at 15.8%, Alphabet at 15.1% and Snap at 10.6% [4]. Its gross margin of 82.0% was the highest, against 80.1% for Pinterest and 59.7% for Alphabet, and its EBITDA margin of 52.6% compared with 44.9% for Alphabet [4]. Its free cash flow conversion of 0.76 also beat Alphabet's 0.55 [4].

The comparison also shows what has weakened. Meta's return on invested capital fell to 22.2% from 29.8%, while Alphabet's was 28.7% [4]. Meta trades at 16.25 times EV/EBITDA against Alphabet's 21.1 times, so it is the cheaper of the two on this measure [4]. Snap's EBITDA was negative in every year, so its multiple is not meaningful, and Pinterest's small EBITDA base makes its 47.81 times multiple a weak comparison [4]. The main points to test against Alphabet's higher returns are Meta's falling ROIC and cash conversion [4].

investment_theses.thesis: Ad pricing and impression growth keep revenue growing near 20% into 2027.
investment_theses.evidence: 2025 revenue grew 22% on 12% more ad impressions and a 9% higher average price per ad [1]. Consensus expects FY2026 revenue growth of 27.8% and FY2027 of 21.9% [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Q4 2026 results (early 2027): ad impressions growth at or above 10% and average price per ad growth at or above 8%.
investment_theses.invalidation: Impressions or price per ad growth below 5% for two consecutive quarters, or FY2027 consensus revenue falling to the bottom of its range [3].

investment_theses.thesis: Free cash flow falls again in 2026 because capex growth outpaces operating cash flow.
investment_theses.evidence: Capex including finance lease principal nearly doubled to $72.22 billion in 2025, and 2026 guidance is $115–135 billion [1]. Holding operating cash flow at the 2025 level leaves about a $9 billion shortfall at the guidance midpoint [1]. Trailing free cash flow was $28.65 billion at 2026-09-30 [2].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 free cash flow reported in the early 2027 10-K is below the 2025 level of $43.59 billion [1].
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2026 free cash flow at or above $43.59 billion, or FY2026 capex below $115 billion [1].

investment_theses.thesis: At the current price, the stock needs growth close to its historical pace, so a fade in consensus growth would push returns below the cost of capital.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 17.7% annual revenue growth for ten years, versus a 19.9% three-year historical CAGR [2][3]. On the consensus path the implied return is 9.7%, below the 11.2% WACC [2][3]. Forward P/E is 21.0x and forward EV/Sales is 6.2x on FY2026E [3].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2027 consensus revenue stays at or above $313 billion (about 22% growth) in the next quarterly consensus updates through Q4 2026 results (early 2027) [3].
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2027 consensus revenue falls to the bottom of its range [3], or the stock re-rates so that the implied return on the consensus path exceeds 11.2% [2][3].

investment_theses.thesis: Reality Labs losses stay near $19 billion a year and cap EPS growth until the AI and hardware payoff is visible.
investment_theses.evidence: Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion from operations in 2025, and management expects 2026 losses to be similar [1]. Current-year EPS consensus fell 8.5% over 90 days to $29.01 [3]. The June and September 2026 quarters missed EPS estimates by 14.4% and 29.3% [3].
investment_theses.signpost: The FY2026 10-K (early 2027) reports a Reality Labs operating loss at or below $19.19 billion [1].
investment_theses.invalidation: The Reality Labs operating loss falls materially below $15 billion, or current-year EPS consensus turns positive over 90 days [1][3].
